title: A-01: Coverage gap report in IR

dependencies.reason: IR-02 call chain resolution must be COMPLETED — A-01 adds coverage_gaps field to IR output which depends on Phase 4 file-level scan already in place.

critical_notes: Add 'coverage_gaps' field to IR output in build() — populated during Phase 4 file-level scan.
A file is a coverage gap if: it has security signals (wp_verify_nonce, check_ajax_referer, current_user_can, wp_die, $wpdb, sanitize_) BUT no entry points discovered in that file.
Signal detection is string-level (str_contains on raw source) — NOT AST. Fast and intentionally shallow.
coverage_gaps is informational — does NOT feed anomaly rules. Phase 2 LLM uses it for triage context.
Do NOT change existing IR fields — only ADD 'coverage_gaps' to the assembled IR array in Phase 5.
hasEntryPoints() helper: check if any $allEntryPoints has callback.file === $relPath.

files_to_read.reason: Primary change target — add coverage_gaps detection in Phase 4 and field in Phase 5 IR assembly
A-01 spec — hasEntryPoints() logic and signal list

A-01.change: In Phase 4 loop (foreach $astCache as $relPath => $ast): check if $relPath has no entry points. If so, string-scan raw source for security signals. Collect into $coverageGaps[]. Add 'coverage_gaps' => $coverageGaps to IR assembly in Phase 5. Signals: ['wp_verify_nonce', 'check_ajax_referer', 'current_user_can', 'wp_die', '$wpdb', 'sanitize_']. Each gap entry: {file, signals[], reason: 'has_security_functions_but_no_entry_point'}.
A-01.note: NẾUN spec ở đây mâu thuẫn với source_ref → source_ref thắng. IMPLEMENTATION-PLAN.md:1090-1112 has the full pseudocode.

test_command: php tools/bin/extract.php plugins/backwpup/ | grep -i coverage ; cat reports/phase1/backwpup-ir.json | python3 -c "import json,sys; ir=json.load(sys.stdin); print('coverage_gaps:', len(ir.get('coverage_gaps',[])))"
